dishes.d: Long-grain rice cooked in a smoky tomato, pepper and onion base, served with chicken.
steps: Season the chicken with salt, thyme and half an onion, then bake or grill at 400°F (200°C) for 30–35 minutes.
Blend the tomatoes, bell peppers, scotch bonnet and one onion until smooth.
Heat the oil, fry the remaining sliced onion for 2 minutes, add the tomato paste and fry 3 minutes until it darkens.
Pour in the blended pepper mix and cook uncovered for 15–20 minutes until reduced and the oil rises to the top.
Add curry, thyme, bay leaves, stock and salt. Stir in the washed rice.
Cover tightly with foil and the lid and cook on low heat for 25–30 minutes, stirring once halfway, until the rice is tender.
Let it rest covered for 5 minutes, then serve with the chicken.
ways: Oven-baked: after step 5, bake covered at 350°F (175°C) for 40 minutes, less stirring and no burning
Swap chicken for grilled fish, turkey, or beans for a vegan version
dishes.pair: Fried or grilled plantain, coleslaw, or a simple cucumber-tomato salad.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days in the fridge or 2 months frozen. Reheat with a splash of water, covered.
light: Use 1 tbsp oil, skinless chicken breast and add mixed vegetables to the rice
prot: Serve with 2 pieces of chicken and a boiled egg

dishes.d: Rice and black-eyed peas cooked together until reddish-brown, with shito, gari, spaghetti, egg and fish on the side.
ing: 6 dried sorghum leaves (waakye leaves), or ¼ tsp baking soda
steps: Drain the soaked peas and boil with the sorghum leaves (or baking soda) in 5 cups of water for 30–40 minutes until almost soft.
Remove the leaves, add the washed rice and salt, and top up water to about 1 inch above the rice.
Cover and cook on low for 20–25 minutes until the rice is soft and the water is absorbed.
Serve with shito, a spoon of gari, boiled egg, and spaghetti or fried fish if you like.
ways: Pressure cooker: peas 10 minutes, then rice 6 minutes
Rice cooker: add par-cooked peas with the rice
dishes.pair: Shito, gari, boiled egg, avocado, fried plantain or fried fish.
dishes.mp: Rice and beans keep 4 days in the fridge; store shito separately. Freeze portions up to 2 months.
light: Skip the spaghetti and gari, use 1 tbsp shito, add a side salad
prot: Add 2 boiled eggs and grilled tilapia

dishes.d: Soft, slightly sour fermented corn and cassava dough with a thick okra stew of fish and meat.
steps: Mix the corn and cassava dough with water and salt until smooth with no lumps.
Cook on medium heat, stirring hard with a wooden spatula, for 15–20 minutes until thick, smooth and stretchy. Shape into balls with a wet bowl.
For the stew: season and boil the meat or fish with onion until tender.
In another pot, heat palm oil, fry the onion and pepper, add the blended tomatoes and cook 10 minutes.
Add the meat, stock and crayfish, then the okra. Cook 5–8 minutes until the okra is soft but still green.
ways: Tomato-only stew with no palm oil
Add kontomire or spinach for more greens
dishes.pair: Pepper sauce (shito or raw pepper), grilled tilapia.
dishes.mp: Okro stew keeps 3 days in the fridge. Wrap banku in plastic and refrigerate up to 3 days; microwave with a damp paper towel.
light: Half a banku ball, extra okra, 1 tbsp oil and fish instead of goat
prot: Double the fish or add crab and shrimp

dishes.d: Grilled whole tilapia with raw pepper sauce and banku, a Ghanaian evening favorite.
ing: 1 banku recipe (see Banku with okro stew)
salt and stock cube to taste
steps: Blend ginger, garlic, half an onion, salt and a little oil. Score the tilapia and rub the marinade inside and out. Rest 30 minutes.
Grill over charcoal or under a broiler, 8–10 minutes per side, until the skin chars and the flesh flakes.
For the pepper sauce, grind (or pulse) tomatoes, peppers and onion with salt. Do not cook it.
Serve the fish with banku and the fresh pepper sauce.
ways: Oven broiler: 12–15 minutes per side on a rack
dishes.pair: Raw pepper sauce (shito or 'moko'), sliced onions.
dishes.mp: Marinate fish up to 24 hours ahead. Grilled fish keeps 2 days; reheat in the oven, not the microwave.
light: Half a banku ball with a large side of cucumber-tomato salad
prot: Keep full banku and add a second small fish

dishes.n: Kenkey with shito and fried fish
dishes.d: Fermented corn dumplings wrapped in husks, eaten with fried fish, shito and fresh pepper.
ing: 4 balls Ga or Fante kenkey (store-bought or homemade)
4 small fish (herring, red fish or tilapia)
steps: Steam or microwave the kenkey in its husk until hot through (about 10 minutes steaming).
Season the fish with salt and fry in hot oil 4–5 minutes per side until crisp, or grill them.
Grind tomatoes, onion, pepper and salt into a fresh pepper sauce.
Unwrap the kenkey and serve with fish, shito and pepper sauce.
ways: Grilled or air-fried fish to cut oil
Homemade kenkey: ferment corn dough 2–3 days, half-cook, wrap in corn husks and boil 2 hours
dishes.pair: Shito, fresh pepper, sliced onions, avocado.
dishes.mp: Kenkey keeps 1 week in the fridge in its husk and freezes well.
light: Half a kenkey ball, grilled fish, skip shito
prot: Add a second fish or boiled eggs

dishes.d: Pounded cassava and plantain with a spicy tomato soup of goat or chicken.
ing: 1 batch fufu (cassava + green plantain, or 2 cups fufu flour)
steps: Season the meat with ginger, garlic, onion and salt and steam in its own juice for 10 minutes.
Add water, whole tomatoes, peppers and the other onion. Boil 15 minutes.
Remove the tomatoes, peppers and onion, blend them, and strain back into the pot.
Simmer 25–30 minutes until the meat is tender and the soup is rich.
For fufu: boil peeled cassava and plantain until soft, then pound (or blend with a little water) until smooth and stretchy. Or stir fufu flour into hot water over low heat until smooth.
ways: Swap goat for chicken, fish or mushrooms
dishes.pair: Any light soup protein: goat, chicken, fish, or 'aponkye' (goat) with 'wele' (cow skin).
dishes.mp: Soup keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes 3 months. Fufu is best fresh but can be wrapped and refrigerated 2 days.
light: Half a fufu ball, chicken breast, extra soup

dishes.d: Creamy peanut soup with chicken or goat, with fufu or omo tuo (rice balls).
ing: 1 cup natural peanut butter (or ground roasted peanuts)
steps: Season the meat with ginger, onion and salt and steam 10 minutes.
Mix the peanut butter with 2 cups of warm water in a separate pot and cook on medium, stirring, for 10 minutes until oil starts to separate.
Add water, tomatoes, peppers and onion to the meat. Boil 15 minutes, then blend the vegetables and return them.
Stir in the cooked peanut paste. Simmer 30–40 minutes until the oil rises to the top.
Serve with fufu or omo tuo.
ways: With omo tuo (mashed soft rice balls)
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes 3 months. It thickens as it cools, so add water when reheating.
light: Use ½ cup peanut butter, chicken breast, half portion of fufu
prot: Add extra chicken and smoked fish

dishes.d: Rich soup from palm fruit concentrate with meat, smoked fish and crab, eaten with fufu or omo tuo.
ing: 1 can (28 oz) palm fruit concentrate (palm butter)
steps: Season and steam the meat with onion, ginger and salt for 10 minutes.
Add water, tomatoes and peppers and boil 15 minutes. Blend the vegetables and return them.
Mix the palm concentrate with 3 cups of water and add to the pot.
Simmer 40–50 minutes, skimming a little oil off the top if you like, until thick.
Add smoked fish and crab for the last 10 minutes.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes well for 3 months.
light: Skim off extra oil, use chicken breast and half portion of fufu

dishes.d: Cocoyam leaf (or spinach) stew with ground egusi and smoked fish, served with yam or plantain.
ing: 1 lb kontomire leaves or spinach, chopped
1 piece smoked fish or salted fish (koobi)
steps: Peel and boil the yam or plantain in salted water for 15–20 minutes until tender.
Heat palm oil, fry the onion, then add blended tomato and pepper and cook 8 minutes.
Mix the egusi with a little water into a paste, add to the pot and cook 5 minutes until it forms curds.
Add the flaked fish and chopped leaves. Stir and cook 5–8 minutes until the leaves wilt.
Add sliced boiled eggs and serve with yam or plantain.
ways: Vegetable oil for a lighter taste
Skip the fish for a vegetarian version with eggs
dishes.pair: Boiled yam, boiled green plantain (ampesi), avocado.
dishes.mp: Stew keeps 3 days in the fridge. Store yam separately.
light: 1 tbsp oil, more leaves, 1 small piece of yam

dishes.d: Black-eyed pea stew in red palm oil with sweet fried plantain on the side.
ing: gari to sprinkle, salt to taste
steps: Boil the soaked peas 40–45 minutes until soft. Drain.
Heat palm oil, fry onion and ginger 2 minutes, add blended tomatoes and pepper and cook 10 minutes.
Add the peas and a splash of water, mash a few, and simmer 10 minutes.
Slice plantains on a diagonal and fry, bake or air-fry until golden.
Serve with gari sprinkled on top.
dishes.mp: Beans keep 5 days in the fridge and freeze 3 months. Cook plantain fresh.
light: 1 tbsp palm oil and air-fried plantain
prot: Add smoked mackerel or a boiled egg on top

dishes.d: Firm corn or millet porridge with a slippery green ayoyo (jute leaf) soup.
steps: Boil 4 cups water, pour in a slurry of 1 cup flour in cold water and stir until it thickens like porridge.
Remove half, add the remaining flour bit by bit to the pot while stirring hard, then add back the porridge to make a smooth, firm dough. Cover and steam 5 minutes.
Boil the meat with onion, tomatoes, pepper and dawadawa until tender.
Boil ayoyo leaves with kanwa for 5 minutes, then whisk until slimy.
Add the ayoyo to the meat soup and simmer 5 minutes.
ways: Millet flour for a nuttier tuo
dishes.mp: Soup keeps 3 days. Tuo is best fresh but keeps 2 days wrapped.

dishes.d: Boiled yam, plantain and cocoyam with a garden egg (African eggplant) stew.
steps: Peel and boil the yam and plantain 15–20 minutes until tender.
Boil the garden eggs 10 minutes, peel and mash.
Fry the onion in oil, add blended tomatoes and pepper and cook 8 minutes.
Stir in the mashed garden eggs and flaked fish or scrambled eggs. Cook 5 minutes.
ways: Roasted yam and plantain in the oven, 425°F (220°C), 25 minutes
dishes.mp: Stew keeps 3 days. Boiled yam keeps 2 days refrigerated.
light: More garden egg stew, smaller portion of yam

dishes.d: Street-style yam chips with shito or fresh pepper sauce.
ing: 4 tbsp shito or fresh pepper sauce
steps: Peel yam and cut into thick fingers. Soak in salted water 10 minutes and dry well.
Fry at 350°F (175°C) for 8–10 minutes until golden outside and soft inside.
Drain and serve with shito or pepper sauce.
ways: Air-fried: toss in 1 tsp oil, 400°F (200°C), 18–20 minutes
dishes.pair: Shito, fried turkey tail, grilled fish, pepper sauce.
dishes.mp: Par-boil and freeze yam fingers, then air-fry from frozen.
prot: Serve with grilled chicken or fried eggs

dishes.d: Spiced millet porridge with ginger and cloves, with koose (bean fritters).
ing: 1 cup fermented millet dough or millet flour
sugar and evaporated milk to taste
steps: Blend or pound ginger, cloves and chili, and mix with the millet and 1 cup cold water.
Bring 3 cups water to a boil, pour in the millet mix while stirring, and cook 8–10 minutes until smooth and thick.
Sweeten to taste and serve with koose and roasted groundnuts.
ways: No sugar, sweetened with a little honey
dishes.mp: Porridge keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat with water.
prot: Stir in 2 tbsp powdered milk and add a boiled egg

dishes.d: Roasted corn and peanut flour porridge, filling and quick.
ing: 1 cup tom brown flour (roasted corn/groundnut blend)
steps: Mix the flour with 1 cup cold water into a smooth paste.
Boil the rest of the water, stir in the paste, and cook 5–7 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Add milk and sugar to taste.
ways: Make a thicker version for toddlers or a thinner drink
dishes.mp: Keep the dry flour in an airtight jar; cook fresh.
prot: Add powdered milk and a spoon of peanut butter

dishes.d: Boiled yam with a tomato and onion scrambled-egg stew.
steps: Peel, cut and boil the yam in salted water for 15–20 minutes.
Fry sliced onion in oil, add chopped tomatoes and pepper and cook 5–7 minutes.
Beat the eggs with salt, pour into the sauce and stir gently until just set.
ways: Sweet potato or plantain in place of yam
dishes.mp: Egg stew keeps 2 days. Boiled yam keeps 2–3 days.
light: Half the yam, 1 tbsp oil, add spinach to the egg stew

dishes.d: Sweet fried plantain with peppery tomato egg sauce.
steps: Slice plantains and fry in hot oil 2–3 minutes per side until golden.
Fry onion, tomato and pepper in 1 tbsp oil for 5 minutes.
Add beaten eggs and scramble gently. Serve with the dodo.
dishes.mp: Make the egg sauce fresh; plantain slices can be air-fried from frozen.
prot: Add a third egg and sardines to the sauce

dishes.d: Ground melon seed soup with leafy greens, meat and stockfish, served with a swallow.
ing: 1.5 lb beef, goat or assorted meat
1 batch pounded yam or poundo flour
steps: Boil the seasoned meat and stockfish with onion until tender. Keep the stock.
Mix egusi with a little water and chopped onion to form a thick paste.
Heat palm oil 2 minutes (don't bleach), drop in spoonfuls of the egusi paste and fry 5 minutes, letting it form lumps.
Add stock, blended pepper, crayfish and iru. Simmer 15 minutes.
Add the meat and greens, cook 5 minutes, and adjust salt.
ways: Smooth egusi: stir the ground seeds straight into the stock
With pounded yam, eba, fufu or rice
dishes.pair: Pounded yam, eba, fufu, semolina, or white rice.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes 3 months. Freeze in single portions.
light: 2 tbsp palm oil, more greens, lean meat, small swallow

dishes.d: Rich spinach stew with peppers, iru, meat and smoked fish.
steps: Blanch the chopped spinach in hot water 1 minute, squeeze out water.
Coarsely blend peppers and one onion; boil down in a pot until most water evaporates.
Heat palm oil, fry sliced onion and iru for 2 minutes, add the pepper mix and fry 10 minutes.
Add crayfish, cooked meat, fish and a splash of stock. Simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in the spinach and cook 3 minutes.
ways: Vegetable oil for a lighter taste
Mushroom version for vegans (skip fish and crayfish)
dishes.pair: White rice, amala, pounded yam, or boiled yam.
dishes.mp: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; freezes 2 months.
light: 1 tbsp palm oil and chicken breast
prot: Add assorted meat and extra fish

dishes.d: Draw soup thickened with ground wild mango seeds, with meat, fish and greens.
steps: Boil the seasoned meat and fish until tender; keep 4 cups of stock.
Warm the palm oil on low, stir in the ogbono until dissolved (1 minute).
Add stock gradually while stirring, then crayfish and pepper. Simmer 10 minutes, stirring so it draws.
Add meat, okra and greens and cook 5 minutes.
ways: With eba, fufu or pounded yam
dishes.mp: Keeps 3 days; freezes 2 months. Reheat gently; it thickens in the fridge.
light: Less oil, more greens, small swallow

dishes.d: Quick draw soup of chopped okra, peppers, fish and greens.
steps: Bring the stock to a boil with onion, crayfish and pepper.
Add the fish and cook 8 minutes.
Add the palm oil and okra and cook 3–4 minutes until it draws but stays green.
Stir in the greens and cook 2 minutes.
dishes.mp: Best within 2 days; freezing softens the okra.
light: Already light: serve with a small swallow or cauliflower 'fufu'

dishes.d: Palm fruit soup spiced with banga spices, with fresh fish, eaten with starch or rice.
ing: 2 tbsp banga spice mix (or oburunbebe stick)
1 tbsp dried bitter leaf or scent leaves
steps: Dilute the palm concentrate with 4 cups of water and bring to a boil.
Add the meat, onion, pepper and crayfish, and cook 20 minutes.
Add banga spices and fish and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the leaves and cook 5 minutes until thick.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days in the fridge; freezes well.
light: Skim oil from the top and use more fish than meat

dishes.d: Hot, aromatic broth with pepper soup spices, goat meat or catfish.
ing: 2 lb goat meat or catfish steaks
steps: Season the meat with onion, ginger and salt; steam 10 minutes.
Add water, pepper and spice mix and simmer 30–35 minutes (catfish: 12 minutes).
Tear in scent leaves in the last 2 minutes.
dishes.pair: Boiled yam, white rice, agidi, or on its own.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days; freezes well.

dishes.d: Steamed savory pudding of blended peeled beans, peppers and onions.
ing: 2 cups black-eyed peas or honey beans, soaked and peeled
steps: Blend the peeled beans with peppers, onion and a little stock until very smooth.
Whisk in oil, the rest of the stock, crayfish and salt to a thick pourable batter.
Pour into greased ramekins, foil packets or leaves; add egg slices.
Steam 45–50 minutes until set and a knife comes out clean.
ways: Baked in a water bath: 350°F (175°C), 50 minutes
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes 3 months in wraps.

dishes.d: Crisp bean fritters (akara or koose) with smooth fermented corn pap.
ing: 2 cups black-eyed peas, soaked and peeled
steps: Blend peas with very little water until thick and smooth. Whisk hard 3–5 minutes to add air.
Stir in chopped onion, pepper and salt.
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil at 350°F (175°C) and fry 3–4 minutes until golden.
For pap: mix ogi with a little cold water, pour in boiling water while stirring until it thickens.
ways: Air-fried akara: spoon onto a greased tray, 375°F (190°C), 12–14 minutes
Baked as akara 'muffins' in a greased tin
dishes.pair: Pap, custard, bread (akara and bread), or koko.
dishes.mp: Batter keeps 1 day refrigerated. Cooked akara reheats in the air fryer in 3 minutes.
prot: Add a boiled egg and milk powder to the pap

dishes.d: Local unpolished rice with 'designer stew', a green pepper stew fried in bleached palm oil.
steps: Wash the rice well and boil 30–35 minutes until tender; drain.
Coarsely blend green peppers and one onion; boil until most of the water evaporates.
Heat the palm oil with the lid on until it turns clear (about 8–10 minutes, with a window open), then let it cool slightly.
Fry sliced onion and iru, add the pepper mix and fry 15 minutes.
Add meat and eggs and simmer 5 minutes.
ways: Vegetable oil for a lighter version
Brown rice if ofada isn't available
dishes.mp: Stew keeps 1 week in the fridge; rice keeps 4 days.
light: Use ¼ cup oil, lean meat, smaller rice portion

dishes.d: Yam flour swallow with jute leaf soup, bean soup and pepper stew ('abula').
ing: 1 cup buka stew (pepper and tomato stew with meat)
steps: Gbegiri: boil peeled beans until very soft, blend smooth, cook with palm oil, pepper, crayfish and salt 10 minutes.
Ewedu: boil leaves with potash 5 minutes, then whisk or pulse until slimy; add iru and salt.
Amala: boil water, stir in yam flour off the heat, then return to low heat and stir hard until smooth. Add a splash of water, cover 2 minutes and stir again.
Serve amala with ewedu, gbegiri and a spoon of stew.
ways: Just ewedu and stew for a lighter plate
dishes.mp: Ewedu and gbegiri keep 3 days; stew 1 week. Make amala fresh.

dishes.d: Yam cubes cooked soft in a palm oil pepper sauce with greens.
steps: Put yam in a pot with water just to cover, add salt and boil 10 minutes.
Add blended tomato and pepper, palm oil, onion and crayfish.
Cook 10–12 minutes until the yam is soft; mash some pieces to thicken.
Stir in spinach and cook 2 minutes.
dishes.pair: Fried fish or a boiled egg.
dishes.mp: Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
light: Half yam, half cauliflower or pumpkin, 1 tbsp oil

dishes.d: Mashed soft beans with a dark, smoky fried-pepper sauce and sweet plantain.
ing: 2 cups honey beans or black-eyed peas
steps: Boil the beans 60–80 minutes until very soft; mash lightly with salt.
Blend the peppers and one onion, and boil off the water.
Heat palm oil, fry sliced onion until very dark, add the pepper mix and fry 15–20 minutes until deep brown.
Fry, bake or air-fry sliced plantain.
Serve beans topped with the sauce and dodo.
dishes.mp: Beans keep 5 days; sauce keeps 2 weeks in the fridge.
light: 2 tbsp oil in the sauce, air-fried plantain
prot: Add a boiled egg or smoked fish

dishes.d: Thin-sliced beef coated in spicy yaji (peanut spice) and grilled, with onion and tomato.
ing: 1.5 lb beef sirloin, very thinly sliced
steps: Toss beef with oil, salt and 3 tbsp yaji. Thread onto soaked skewers. Rest 30 minutes.
Grill over high heat 3–4 minutes per side.
Dust with the remaining yaji and serve with onion and tomato.
dishes.mp: Marinate up to 24 hours. Cooked suya keeps 3 days; reheat in the air fryer.
prot: Larger portion with a side of eggs

dishes.d: Curry-seasoned rice stir-fried with liver, mixed vegetables and shrimp.
ing: 1 cup mixed veg (carrots, peas, green beans)
steps: Cook the rice in stock with curry, thyme and salt until just tender, about 15 minutes. Spread out to cool.
Fry the diced liver or shrimp in 1 tbsp oil and set aside.
Stir-fry onion and vegetables 3 minutes in the remaining oil.
Add the rice in batches with the liver/shrimp and toss 3–4 minutes on high heat.
ways: Sheet pan in the oven at 425°F (220°C) for 15 minutes
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes well.
light: More vegetables than rice, 1 tbsp oil

dishes.d: Senegal's national dish: fish stuffed with parsley-garlic rof, cooked with vegetables, then broken rice cooked in the broth.
ing: 2 lb firm white fish steaks (grouper or snapper)
steps: Pound parsley, garlic, pepper and salt (rof). Cut slits in the fish and stuff with rof.
Fry the onions in oil, add tomato paste and fry 5 minutes. Add 6 cups water and the dried fish.
Add the vegetables and fish; simmer 25–30 minutes until tender. Lift everything out and keep warm.
Measure 4 cups of broth into the pot, add washed rice, cover and cook on low 25–30 minutes.
Serve rice with the fish and vegetables on top; the crispy bottom (xoon) is a treat.
dishes.pair: Lime wedges, extra rof, hot pepper sauce.
dishes.mp: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; store rice and fish together.
light: More vegetables, less rice and oil

dishes.d: Chicken marinated in lemon, mustard and a mountain of onions, grilled and braised.
steps: Marinate chicken with onions, lemon, mustard, garlic, pepper and salt for at least 2 hours (overnight is best).
Grill or broil the chicken until charred, 8–10 minutes per side.
Cook the onions from the marinade in oil for 15 minutes until soft and golden.
Add chicken, remaining marinade, bay leaves and 1 cup water. Simmer 20 minutes.
Serve over rice.
ways: All in the oven: roast chicken on the onions at 400°F (200°C) for 45 minutes
dishes.mp: Better the next day. Keeps 4 days; freezes 2 months.
light: Skinless chicken, 1 tbsp oil, half the rice

dishes.d: Beef or chicken simmered in a tomato-peanut sauce with root vegetables.
steps: Brown the meat in oil, add onion and garlic and cook 3 minutes.
Add tomato paste and fry 2 minutes, then water and the whole pepper.
Whisk in the peanut butter and simmer 30 minutes.
Add vegetables and cook 20 minutes until tender and the oil rises.
ways: Vegan with chickpeas and extra vegetables
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days; freezes 3 months.
light: ½ cup peanut butter, chicken breast, more vegetables

dishes.d: The Gambia's peanut stew with pumpkin and a squeeze of lime.
steps: Brown the meat and onion in oil.
Add tomato paste, water and pepper and cook 20 minutes.
Stir in peanut paste and pumpkin and simmer 25 minutes until thick.
Finish with lime juice.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days; freezes well.

dishes.d: One-pot rice cooked in a spiced tomato stock with meat or fish and vegetables. The Gambia's cousin of jollof.
steps: Brown the seasoned meat in oil, remove.
Fry onion and tomato paste 5 minutes, add stock, vegetables and meat, and simmer 20 minutes.
Remove the vegetables, add the rice and cook covered on low 25 minutes.
Serve with the vegetables on top.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

dishes.d: Fluffy fermented cassava couscous with grilled fish, tomato-onion salad and chili.
steps: Marinate the fish in garlic, oil, salt and lime for 20 minutes.
Grill 8–10 minutes per side.
Steam or microwave the attiéké 3–5 minutes, fluffing with a fork.
Dice tomato, onion, cucumber and pepper with lime and salt for the salad.
ways: Grilled fish (garba style uses fried tuna)
dishes.mp: Frozen attiéké keeps 3 months; fish marinade can be made 1 day ahead.

dishes.d: Chicken slow-cooked in a sealed pot with its own juices, tomato, eggplant and pepper.
steps: Put everything in a heavy pot, no water.
Seal with the lid (or foil under the lid) and cook on low for 50–60 minutes.
Shake the pot every 10 minutes instead of opening it.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days and freezes well.

dishes.d: Finely pounded cassava leaves simmered with palm oil, smoked fish and meat.
steps: Boil the cassava leaves in water for 30 minutes.
Boil the seasoned meat with onion until tender.
Add meat, stock, smoked fish, pepper and palm oil to the leaves.
Simmer 30 minutes until thick, adding peanut butter if using.
Serve over rice.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days and freezes 3 months.
light: ¼ cup palm oil, chicken, smaller rice portion

dishes.d: Sweet potato leaves cooked with palm oil, meat and smoked fish.
steps: Cook the seasoned meat with onion until tender.
Add palm oil and pepper, cook 5 minutes.
Add the finely chopped leaves and smoked fish, and cook 15 minutes.
Serve over rice.
ways: Spinach when potato leaves aren't available
dishes.mp: Keeps 3 days; freezes well.
light: Less oil, chicken, small rice portion

dishes.d: Light ancient-grain salad with tomato, cucumber, herbs, lime and roasted groundnuts.
steps: Bring water and salt to a boil, stir in fonio, cover and cook 1–2 minutes. Rest 5 minutes and fluff.
Dice the vegetables and chop the herbs.
Toss with lime, oil, salt and peanuts.
ways: Warm fonio as a rice replacement
dishes.mp: Keeps 3 days; add herbs fresh.

dishes.d: Gari moistened and stirred into an egg and tomato stew; a quick, budget lunch.
steps: Sprinkle the gari with a little salted warm water to moisten. Fluff.
Fry onion in oil, add tomatoes and pepper and cook 5 minutes.
Add the eggs (and sardines) and scramble.
Stir in the gari until well combined.
dishes.mp: Best fresh; keeps 1 day.
prot: Add sardines and an extra egg

dishes.d: Spiced red lentil stew with berbere, eaten with sour teff flatbread.
steps: Cook onions in a dry pot 5 minutes, then add oil, garlic and ginger.
Add berbere and cook 2 minutes.
Add lentils and water and simmer 25–30 minutes until thick.
Serve on injera.
ways: Yellow split pea kik alicha for a mild version
dishes.mp: Keeps 5 days and freezes well.
prot: Add doro wot chicken or hard-boiled eggs

dishes.d: Firm white-corn meal with sautéed collard greens and tomato; add beef or fish.
steps: Boil water, add flour gradually while stirring hard until thick and pulling from the sides (8–10 minutes).
Fry onion and tomato 5 minutes, add finely sliced greens and cook 5 minutes.
Serve ugali with the greens and meat or fish.
ways: With nyama choma or fried fish
dishes.mp: Greens keep 3 days; make ugali fresh.

dishes.d: Spiced rice with cumin, cardamom and cloves cooked with beef or chicken.
steps: Fry onions in oil until dark brown.
Add garlic, ginger, masala and meat and cook 10 minutes.
Add potatoes and stock and simmer 10 minutes.
Add rice, cover and cook on low 20 minutes.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

dishes.d: Corn and beans stewed with onions, tomatoes and potatoes.
ing: 1.5 cups dried corn (or 1 can sweet corn)
steps: Boil soaked corn and beans until tender (about 1 hour), or use canned.
Fry onion, tomatoes and curry 5 minutes.
Add the corn, beans, potatoes and a cup of water and cook 15 minutes.
dishes.mp: Keeps 5 days and freezes well.

dishes.d: Steamed couscous under a broth of seven vegetables and chickpeas.
steps: Sauté onion in oil, add spices and tomatoes and cook 3 minutes.
Add stock and root vegetables and simmer 20 minutes; add zucchini and chickpeas for the last 10.
Pour boiling water over couscous (equal amount), cover 5 minutes and fluff.
Serve vegetables and broth over couscous.
dishes.mp: Broth keeps 4 days; store couscous separately.

dishes.d: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce.
steps: Cook onion and peppers in oil 6 minutes, add garlic and spices.
Add tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes.
Make wells and crack in the eggs. Cover and cook 5–7 minutes.
dishes.mp: Make the sauce up to 4 days ahead; add eggs fresh.

dishes.d: Warm stewed fava beans with cumin, lemon, garlic and olive oil.
steps: Warm the beans with their liquid 10 minutes, mashing some.
Stir in garlic, cumin, lemon and salt.
Top with oil, tomato and parsley.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days.

dishes.n: Chicken tagine with olives and lemon
dishes.d: Slow-cooked chicken with preserved lemon, olives, ginger and saffron.
steps: Rub chicken with spices, garlic and oil; marinate 1 hour.
Cook onions and chicken in a tagine or heavy pot with a cup of water, covered, 45 minutes on low.
Add olives and lemon for the last 15 minutes. Finish with cilantro.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days; freezes well.

dishes.d: Bitterleaf and peanut stew with beef and shrimp, Cameroon's national dish.
ing: 1.5 cups raw peanuts, boiled and blended
steps: Boil beef with onion, garlic and ginger until tender.
Add the peanut paste and simmer 20 minutes, stirring.
Add the bitterleaf and cook 10 minutes.
Fry shrimp and onion in oil separately and add on top.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days and freezes well.

dishes.d: Cassava leaves slow-cooked with onions, eggplant, palm oil and smoked fish.
steps: Boil cassava leaves 30 minutes.
Add onion, eggplant, garlic and fish and cook 20 minutes.
Stir in palm oil and simmer 10 minutes.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days; freezes well.

dishes.d: Chicken stewed in palm butter sauce with tomato and onion.
steps: Brown chicken, add onion, garlic, tomato and chili.
Stir in palm butter with 2 cups water.
Simmer 40 minutes until thick.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days and freezes well.

dishes.d: Stiff maize porridge with a spicy bean and vegetable relish; often with boerewors.
steps: Boil water with salt, add maize meal, stir, cover and cook 20 minutes, stirring now and then.
Fry onion, pepper and curry, add carrots and tomatoes and cook 8 minutes.
Stir in the beans and heat through.
dishes.mp: Chakalaka keeps 5 days.

dishes.d: Curried minced beef with dried fruit, baked under an egg custard.
steps: Brown onion and beef, add spices, chutney, raisins and squeezed bread.
Spread in a baking dish.
Whisk eggs and milk, pour over, add bay leaves.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) 30–35 minutes until set.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days; freezes well.

dishes.d: Firm maize meal with muriwo (greens, optionally with peanut butter) and beans.
ing: 1 can sugar beans or kidney beans
steps: Make sadza like ugali: porridge first, then add meal until firm.
Fry onion and tomato, add greens and cook 5 minutes; stir in peanut butter if using.
Warm the beans with a little onion.
dishes.mp: Greens and beans keep 4 days.

dishes.d: Rice and black beans fried with onion, pepper and cilantro, with eggs.
steps: Sauté onion and pepper 5 minutes.
Add beans with a little liquid, then the rice; toss 5 minutes.
Finish with cilantro. Serve with fried or scrambled eggs.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days.

dishes.n: Rice and peas with jerk chicken
dishes.d: Coconut rice with kidney beans and thyme, with spicy grilled jerk chicken.
steps: Marinate the chicken in jerk seasoning 4+ hours.
Grill or bake at 400°F (200°C) 35–40 minutes.
Simmer beans, coconut milk, water, scallion, thyme and whole scotch bonnet; add rice, cover and cook 20 minutes.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days.

dishes.d: Yellow lentils with turmeric, finished with a sizzling tempering of cumin and garlic.
steps: Boil lentils with turmeric until soft, 20–25 minutes.
Fry cumin, garlic, onion and tomato in oil; pour into the dal.
Serve with rice.
dishes.mp: Keeps 5 days; freezes well.

dishes.n: Salmon with sweet potato and greens
dishes.d: Sheet-pan salmon with roasted sweet potato and green beans.
steps: Roast cubed sweet potato with 1 tbsp oil at 425°F (220°C) for 15 minutes.
Add green beans and salmon, season, drizzle oil.
Roast 10–12 more minutes.
dishes.mp: Keeps 3 days.

dishes.d: Oats cooked in milk with banana and peanut butter.
steps: Simmer oats in milk 5 minutes.
Top with sliced banana, peanut butter and cinnamon.
dishes.mp: Overnight oats keep 4 days.
light: Water instead of milk, 1 tbsp PB
prot: Add Greek yogurt or protein powder

dishes.d: Spiced chicken, rice, beans, salsa and avocado in a bowl.
steps: Season and grill or pan-fry chicken 6 minutes per side; slice.
Warm beans and corn.
Build bowls with rice, beans, corn, chicken, salsa and avocado.
dishes.mp: Prep components; keeps 4 days (add avocado fresh).
prot: Extra chicken, Greek yogurt as sour cream

dishes.d: Three-egg omelet with spinach, peppers, onion and cheese.
steps: Soften the vegetables in butter 3 minutes.
Pour in beaten eggs and cook until almost set.
Add cheese, fold and serve.
dishes.mp: Egg muffins keep 4 days.

dishes.d: Efik vegetable soup packed with pumpkin leaves, waterleaf, meat and fish, served with pounded yam.
ing: 1 lb beef and cow skin (ponmo), cut up
1 batch pounded yam or poundo flour
steps: Boil the seasoned beef, cow skin and stockfish with onion until tender. Keep about 1 cup of the stock.
Wash the waterleaf, squeeze out the water and add it to the pot with the palm oil. Cook 5 minutes without stirring much.
Add the stock, crayfish, pepper, smoked fish and salt. Simmer 5 minutes.
Fold in the ugu and cook 3 minutes only so the leaves stay bright and the soup stays thick, not watery.
Serve with pounded yam.
ways: Swap the beef for extra fish for a lighter pot
dishes.pair: Pounded yam, eba, fufu or semolina.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes 3 months. Freeze without the swallow.
light: Use 2 tbsp palm oil, drop the cow skin and take a smaller swallow
prot: Add a second portion of meat and fish

dishes.d: Igbo soup of oha leaves thickened with cocoyam, with meat, stockfish and palm oil.
ing: 4 cups oha leaves, torn (or spinach and a little scent leaf)
1 lb beef or goat, cut up
1 batch pounded yam or poundo flour
steps: Boil the seasoned meat and stockfish until tender. Keep the stock.
Add the mashed cocoyam to the stock and stir until it dissolves into a light thickener.
Add palm oil, crayfish and ground pepper and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the oha leaves and cook 3 minutes. Don't overcook or the colour and flavour dull.
Adjust salt and serve with pounded yam.
ways: Use spinach and scent leaf if oha leaves aren't available
dishes.pair: Pounded yam, fufu, eba or akpu.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes 3 months in single portions.
light: Use 2 tbsp palm oil, lean meat and a smaller swallow
prot: Add fish or an extra portion of meat

dishes.d: Igbo soup of washed bitterleaf in a cocoyam-thickened palm oil base with meat and fish.
ing: 1 lb assorted meat and cow skin
steps: Wash the bitterleaf in several changes of water, squeezing well, until the bitterness is mild.
Boil the seasoned meat and stockfish until tender, then add the mashed cocoyam to thicken the stock.
Add palm oil, crayfish, pepper and fish and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the washed bitterleaf and cook 5 minutes.
Adjust salt and serve with fufu or pounded yam.
ways: Classic with fufu or pounded yam
Wash the leaves less for a more bitter, traditional taste
dishes.pair: Fufu, pounded yam, eba or akpu.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes 3 months in single portions.
light: Use 2 tbsp palm oil, lean meat and a smaller swallow

dishes.d: Grated water yam cooked into a thick, peppery porridge with smoked fish and palm oil.
ing: 1.5 lb water yam, peeled and grated
steps: Heat the palm oil gently, add sliced onion and blended pepper and fry 5 minutes.
Add the stock, crayfish, smoked and dried fish and bring to a simmer.
Drop in the grated yam in spoonfuls so it forms small lumps. Do not stir for the first 5 minutes.
Cover and cook on low heat 20–25 minutes, stirring gently, until the yam is cooked through and thick.
Adjust salt and serve hot.
ways: Use fresh fish and prawns on top
dishes.pair: Eaten on its own; a side of ripe plantain works.
dishes.mp: Keeps 3 days in the fridge. It thickens, so loosen with stock when reheating.
light: Use 2 tbsp palm oil and add leafy greens

dishes.d: Clear, peppery Niger Delta soup of fresh fish and prawns scented with uziza and scent leaf.
ing: 2 lb assorted fresh fish (catfish, tilapia, croaker)
1 cup scent leaf or uziza leaves, torn
4 cups water or light fish stock
steps: Bring the water or stock to a boil with sliced onion, pepper, salt and stock cube.
Add the fish in large pieces and simmer 8 minutes.
Add the prawns, crayfish, uziza seed and palm oil and cook 5 minutes.
Add the scent leaf and turn off the heat.
Taste for pepper and salt and serve in bowls.
ways: Add periwinkle or crab if you like
Make it milder with fewer peppers
dishes.pair: Eaten on its own; a small portion of boiled yam or plantain works.
dishes.mp: Best fresh. Keeps 2 days in the fridge and doesn't freeze well.
light: Use 1 tbsp palm oil and more leaf

dishes.d: Chicken gizzards simmered tender and tossed in a peppery tomato sauce with fried ripe plantain.
steps: Boil the gizzards with onion, salt and stock cube 30–40 minutes until tender.
Blend the peppers, scotch bonnet and half the onion and cook down until thick.
Fry the plantain cubes in a little oil until golden and drain well, or air-fry at 400°F (200°C) for 12 minutes.
Fry the sliced onion in 1 tbsp oil, add the pepper sauce, curry and thyme and cook 8 minutes.
Add the gizzards and plantain and toss until coated.
ways: Add a splash of stock for a saucier version
dishes.pair: Eaten alone or with a side salad.
dishes.mp: Gizzards and sauce keep 3 days. Fry fresh plantain when serving.
light: Air-fry the plantain and use 2 tbsp oil
prot: Add a hard-boiled egg or extra gizzards

dishes.d: Steamed bean pudding without oil, served with a smoky pepper sauce.
steps: Soak and peel the beans, then blend with a little water to a thick smooth paste.
Season with salt and scoop into leaves, ramekins or foil and tie or cover.
Steam 45–60 minutes until firm.
For the sauce, blend peppers and half the onion and cook down until thick. Heat the palm oil, fry the rest of the onion, add the pepper and cook 10 minutes.
Serve the ekuru with the sauce.
ways: Add a boiled egg on the side
dishes.pair: Ewa agoyin sauce, fried fish or boiled egg.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes 2 months.
light: Use 1 tbsp palm oil in the sauce
prot: Serve with a boiled egg and fish

dishes.d: Fermented rice cakes pan-fried until crisp outside and soft inside, with spicy yaji.
ing: 2 tbsp vegetable oil, for the pan
steps: Blend the soaked rice, cooked rice and a little water to a smooth thick batter.
Stir in yeast and sugar, cover and rest 3–4 hours until bubbly.
Add salt and baking powder and mix.
Heat an oiled masa pan and pour in small rounds. Cover and cook 3 minutes, flip, cook 2 minutes more until golden.
Serve with yaji and sliced onion.
ways: Air-fry in a lightly oiled mould for less oil
dishes.mp: The batter keeps 1 day in the fridge. Cooked masa keeps 2 days.
light: Use less oil in the pan
prot: Serve with a boiled egg or akara

dishes.d: Steamed Bambara nut pudding coloured and enriched with palm oil.
steps: Whisk the flour with warm water to a smooth, slightly thick batter, no lumps.
Stir in palm oil, onion, pepper, crayfish, salt and stock cube until the batter turns orange.
Pour into leaves, foil or small containers.
Steam 45–60 minutes until firm and set.
Cool a few minutes before unwrapping.
ways: Omit crayfish for a fully vegan version
dishes.pair: Pap, a boiled egg or fried fish.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes 2 months wrapped.
prot: Serve with a boiled egg and fish

dishes.d: Igbo delicacy of tender goat head in a palm oil and utazi sauce.
ing: 2.5 lb goat head, cleaned and cut
steps: Boil the seasoned goat head with salt and stock cube 60–90 minutes until very tender.
Dissolve the potash in 2 tbsp water, let it settle and pour off the clear water. Mix with the palm oil until creamy.
Add crayfish and pepper to the palm oil mix.
Toss the warm meat with the mix and sliced onion.
Top with utazi leaves and serve.
ways: Use goat ribs if you cannot get the head
Pressure-cook to cut the time to 35 minutes
dishes.pair: Cold beer or palm wine is traditional; try zobo for a soft drink.
dishes.mp: Keeps 3 days in the fridge. Reheat the meat gently and dress fresh.
light: Skim fat from the meat and use 2 tbsp palm oil
prot: Serve with a side of ugba or beans

dishes.d: Fanti fisherman's stew of fresh fish in a ginger and tomato sauce.
ing: 1.5 lb fresh fish (tilapia or mackerel), cut
steps: Season the fish with salt, ginger and half the onion.
Blend the tomatoes, pepper and the rest of the onion.
Heat the oil and fry the tomato paste 2 minutes, then add the blended mix and cook 12 minutes until thick.
Lay the fish in the sauce, cover and simmer 10 minutes without stirring much.
Adjust salt and serve.
ways: Use vegetable oil for a lighter stew
Add okra in the last 5 minutes
dishes.pair: Kenkey, banku, boiled yam, plantain or rice (add about 200–300 calories for the starch).
dishes.mp: Keeps 3 days in the fridge and freezes 2 months.
light: Use 2 tbsp oil and skinless fish

dishes.d: Ewe dish of soft maize and cassava dough balls with light okra soup and smoked fish.
steps: Blend tomato, onion and pepper and simmer with water 10 minutes.
Add the smoked fish, palm oil and okra and cook 8 minutes. Add salt.
For akple, mix the two doughs with water, cook over medium heat stirring hard until thick, then cover and steam 5 minutes.
Stir and shape into smooth balls.
Serve the akple with the soup.
ways: Serve the soup with banku or rice instead
dishes.mp: Soup keeps 3 days. Make akple fresh.
light: Use 2 tbsp palm oil and a smaller akple ball
prot: Add a piece of grilled fish

dishes.d: Mashed ripe plantain stirred with palm oil, topped with boiled eggs.
steps: Peel the plantains, cut into chunks and boil 15 minutes until soft.
Drain and mash with salt until chunky-smooth.
Warm the palm oil with the onion and stir through the mash.
Season with pepper if you like.
Top with halved boiled eggs.
ways: Serve with avocado for extra fat and fibre
dishes.pair: Avocado, kontomire stew or tomato stew.
dishes.mp: Keeps 2 days in the fridge. Reheat with a splash of water.
prot: Use 6 eggs between four servings or add avocado

dishes.d: Ivorian street staple of steamed cassava couscous, fried tuna and a fresh tomato and onion salad.
steps: Steam the attiéké according to the packet and fluff with a fork.
Season the tuna with salt and pepper and fry 3–4 minutes a side in a little oil until just cooked.
Mix the tomatoes, onions, chopped pepper and lime juice with a pinch of salt.
Plate the attiéké with the fish and top with the salad.
Serve hot with extra pepper.
dishes.pair: Pepper sauce or a boiled egg.
dishes.mp: Cook fresh. The fish keeps 2 days in the fridge.
light: Grill the tuna and take a smaller portion of attiéké

dishes.d: Marinated chicken grilled until charred, with fried ripe plantain and onion sauce.
steps: Marinate the chicken with garlic, ginger, mustard, lime, stock cube and half the onion for at least 1 hour.
Grill or bake at 425°F (220°C) for 35–40 minutes, turning once, until charred and cooked through.
Slice the plantain and fry in hot oil 2–3 minutes a side until golden and drain, or air-fry at 400°F (200°C) for 12 minutes.
Cook the remaining onion in 1 tbsp oil with a splash of water into a soft sauce.
Serve the chicken with plantain and onion sauce.
dishes.mp: Chicken keeps 3 days. Fry the plantain fresh.
light: Use skinless chicken and air-fry the plantain
prot: Add a second piece of chicken

dishes.d: Rice cooked in a rich tomato and vegetable stock with beef and vegetables.
steps: Brown the beef in oil, add onion and garlic and cook 3 minutes.
Add blended tomato and tomato paste and cook 10 minutes until the oil rises.
Add stock, carrots and cabbage and simmer 15 minutes.
Remove the meat and vegetables and keep warm. Add washed rice to the stock.
Cover and cook on low heat 20 minutes, then serve with the meat and vegetables on top.
dishes.mp: Keeps 3 days in the fridge and freezes 2 months.
light: Use 2 tbsp oil and more vegetables
prot: Add extra meat or an egg

dishes.d: Sahel staple: a firm millet or sorghum paste with a sticky okra sauce and smoked fish.
ing: 2 tbsp vegetable oil or shea oil
steps: Fry the onion in oil, add chopped tomato and cook 5 minutes.
Add 2 cups water, salt, soumbala and fish and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the okra and cook 8 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Stir the flour into 2 cups boiling water on low heat, beating hard with a wooden spoon until smooth and firm.
Shape into balls and serve with the sauce.
ways: Add dried beef or chicken to the sauce
dishes.mp: Sauce keeps 3 days. Make tô fresh.
light: Use 1 tbsp oil and a smaller tô

dishes.n: Fried yam with wagashi and tomato sauce
dishes.d: Beninese street snack turned meal: fried yam with golden fried wagashi cheese and spicy tomato sauce.
ing: 2 lb yam, peeled and cut in batons
8 oz wagashi, or firm cheese such as halloumi or paneer
steps: Boil the yam 8 minutes in salted water, drain and dry.
Fry the yam in hot oil until golden and drain, or air-fry at 400°F (200°C) for 20 minutes.
Fry the cheese cubes in a little oil until crisp outside.
Blend the tomato, pepper and half the onion. Fry the rest of the onion, add paste and the blend and cook 12 minutes.
Serve the yam and cheese with the sauce.
ways: Use fried tofu to make it vegan
dishes.mp: Sauce keeps 3 days. Fry yam and cheese fresh.
light: Air-fry the yam and use 1 tbsp oil in the sauce

dishes.n: Amiwo (red maize pâte) with fish stew
dishes.d: Beninese red maize pâte cooked in tomato and palm oil, with a fish stew.
ing: 1.5 lb tilapia or other fresh fish
steps: Blend tomato, onion and pepper and cook down with the tomato paste and palm oil 12 minutes.
Remove a third of the sauce and set aside for the fish.
Add 3 cups water to the rest and bring to a boil, then stir in the maize flour gradually, beating until it forms a smooth firm pâte.
Cover and steam on low heat 5 minutes.
Gently simmer the fish in the reserved sauce 10 minutes and serve with the amiwo.
ways: With a vegetable sauce for a vegan version
dishes.pair: Pepper sauce, fried fish or gombo sauce.
dishes.mp: The fish stew keeps 3 days. Make the pâte fresh.
light: Use 2 tbsp palm oil and a smaller portion of pâte
prot: Add a second piece of fish

dishes.n: Grilled fish with aloko and pili-pili
dishes.d: Togolese and Beninese evening meal: grilled fish, fried ripe plantain (aloko) and a hot pili-pili sauce.
steps: Season the fish with salt, ginger and lime juice and rest 15 minutes.
Grill or pan-sear the fish 4 minutes a side.
Slice the plantain and fry 2–3 minutes a side until golden and drain, or air-fry at 400°F (200°C) for 12 minutes.
For pili-pili, finely chop the pepper, tomato and onion and mix with a spoon of hot oil and salt.
Serve the fish with aloko and the sauce.
dishes.mp: Fish keeps 2 days. Fry the plantain fresh.
light: Air-fry the plantain and grill the fish with no oil

dishes.d: Sahel breakfast of spiced millet balls in fermented milk.
ing: 3 cups nono (fermented milk) or plain yogurt
steps: Mix the millet flour with ginger, cloves, salt and just enough water to form a stiff dough.
Roll into small balls and steam or boil 15 minutes until cooked.
Break the balls and mash them smooth with a little water to make the fura.
Spoon into bowls and top with the milk.
Add sugar if you like and serve.
ways: Use unsweetened yogurt for a milder taste
Add dates for sweetness instead of sugar
dishes.mp: The fura balls keep 2 days in the fridge. Add the milk fresh.
light: Use unsweetened yogurt and skip the sugar
prot: Use Greek yogurt for extra protein

dishes.d: Mauritanian couscous steamed over a lamb and vegetable stew.
steps: Brown the lamb with onion in oil, add the spices and stock and simmer 40 minutes.
Add carrots, turnips, cabbage and chickpeas and cook 15 minutes.
Moisten the couscous with a little water, salt and a drizzle of oil and rub until fluffy.
Steam the couscous 10 minutes, or soak in boiling stock 5 minutes and fluff.
Serve the stew over the couscous.
dishes.pair: Harissa or a squeeze of lemon.
dishes.mp: Keeps 3 days in the fridge. Store the stew and couscous separately.
light: Use a smaller portion of couscous and more vegetables

dishes.d: Slow-cooked national dish of hominy, beans, pork and sausage with cassava and sweet potato.
ing: 0.75 cup dried beans (kidney or lima), soaked overnight
steps: Cook the soaked hominy and beans with bay leaves in plenty of water for 1 hour 15 minutes until nearly tender.
Brown the pork and sausage in oil with onion and garlic.
Add them to the pot with the cassava and sweet potato and cook 20 minutes.
Add the cabbage and cook 10 minutes more. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot. Leftovers are traditionally fried for breakfast.
ways: Pressure-cook the beans and hominy to save time
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes 2 months. Reheated cachupa fried in a pan is a classic breakfast.
light: Use less sausage and more vegetables

dishes.d: Bissau-Guinean chicken stewed in a thick peanut sauce, served over rice.
steps: Brown the chicken in oil, then set aside. Cook the onion and garlic in the same pot 3 minutes.
Add the blended tomato and pepper and cook 8 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter into the stock and add to the pot with the chicken.
Simmer 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the chicken is tender and the sauce thickens.
Cook the rice and serve the stew over it.
ways: Add pumpkin or cassava for body
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes 3 months.
light: Use skinless chicken and a smaller rice portion

dishes.d: Senegalese okra stew with palm oil, fresh and smoked fish, served over rice.
steps: Fry the onion in palm oil for 3 minutes and add the tomato paste. Cook 3 minutes.
Add the stock, smoked fish, pepper and salt and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the okra and cook 10 minutes until the stew thickens.
Slide in the fresh fish and cook 8 minutes without stirring hard.
Cook the rice and serve the stew over it.
ways: Classic with fresh and smoked fish
Use vegetable oil instead of palm oil
dishes.mp: Keeps 3 days in the fridge and freezes 2 months.
light: Use 2 tbsp palm oil and a smaller rice portion

dishes.d: West African leafy sauce of spinach or cocoyam leaves with beef, smoked fish and palm oil.
ing: 2 lb spinach or cocoyam leaves, chopped
steps: Boil the beef with onion, salt and stock cube until tender.
Add the palm oil, crayfish, pepper and smoked fish and simmer 5 minutes.
Add the leaves and cook 15–20 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and the oil rises.
Taste for salt and pepper.
Cook the rice and serve the sauce over it.
ways: Use spinach if cocoyam leaves aren't available
dishes.pair: White rice, cassava or boiled yam.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes 3 months.
light: Use 2 tbsp palm oil and a smaller rice portion

dishes.n: Baked fish and chips with mushy peas
dishes.d: A lighter take on the takeaway classic: crumb-coated cod, oven chips and mushy peas.
steps: Toss the chips with oil and salt and roast at 425°F (220°C) for 35 minutes, turning once.
Dip the fish in flour, then egg, then panko. Place on a lined tray.
Bake the fish for the last 15–18 minutes until golden and flaking.
Simmer the peas 4 minutes, drain, add butter and mash roughly with salt and a squeeze of lemon.
Mix the mayonnaise with gherkins for tartare sauce and serve everything together.
ways: Air-fry the fish and chips at 400°F (200°C)
Use skinless chicken for fish-free nights
dishes.pair: Lemon, malt vinegar and tartare sauce.
dishes.mp: Best fresh. Fish keeps 2 days in the fridge.
light: Use 1 tbsp oil for the chips and skip the butter
prot: Add a second piece of fish

dishes.d: Eggs, back bacon, sausage, beans, mushrooms, tomato and toast, grilled rather than fried.
steps: Grill the sausages 12–15 minutes, turning, and add the bacon for the last 5 minutes.
Brush the mushrooms and tomato halves with oil and grill alongside 6–8 minutes.
Warm the beans in a small pan.
Poach, boil or fry the eggs to your liking.
Toast the bread and plate everything.
ways: Swap sausage for extra mushrooms and beans
dishes.mp: Cook fresh. Beans and sausages reheat well for 2 days.
light: Use 1 egg, 1 rasher and skip the sausage

dishes.d: Britain's favourite curry: marinated grilled chicken in a creamy spiced tomato sauce.
ing: 0.5 cup single cream or coconut cream
steps: Marinate the chicken in yogurt, half the spice mix and salt for at least 30 minutes.
Grill or bake the chicken at 450°F (230°C) for 12–15 minutes until charred.
Cook the onion, garlic and ginger in oil and butter 6 minutes, add the rest of the spices and tomatoes and simmer 12 minutes.
Blend the sauce until smooth, stir in the cream and chicken and simmer 5 minutes.
Cook the rice and serve with coriander.
ways: Swap chicken for paneer or chickpeas
dishes.pair: Basmati rice, naan or roti, a cucumber raita.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes 3 months without the rice.
light: Use half the cream and a smaller portion of rice

dishes.n: Sunday roast chicken with roast potatoes and vegetables
dishes.d: Roast chicken with crisp roast potatoes, vegetables and gravy.
steps: Season the chicken with butter, salt, pepper and thyme and roast at 400°F (200°C) for 1 hour 15 minutes until the juices run clear. Rest 15 minutes.
Parboil the potatoes 8 minutes, drain, shake to rough up and roast in hot oil for 45 minutes, turning once.
Roast or steam the carrots and broccoli until just tender.
Make gravy from the roasting pan juices, stock and cornflour.
Carve and serve.
ways: Skip the skin for fewer calories
dishes.mp: Leftover chicken keeps 3 days and makes sandwiches or soup.
light: Remove the skin and use 1 tbsp oil on the potatoes
prot: Add a second portion of chicken

dishes.d: Scottish smoked haddock and potato soup.
steps: Simmer the haddock in the milk and water 6 minutes, then lift out, flake and discard skin and bones.
Cook the onion in butter 4 minutes, add the potatoes and the poaching liquid and simmer 15 minutes.
Mash roughly some of the potato in the pot to thicken.
Return the fish and warm through.
Season with pepper and add herbs.
ways: Use semi-skimmed milk for a lighter soup
dishes.mp: Keeps 3 days in the fridge. Don't boil after adding fish.
light: Use semi-skimmed milk and skip the butter
prot: Serve with a slice of rye or wholegrain bread

dishes.d: Slow-cooked oats with milk, berries and a little honey.
steps: Combine the oats, milk and salt in a pan.
Bring to a gentle boil, stirring.
Simmer 5–8 minutes until thick and creamy.
Spoon into bowls.
Top with berries and honey.
ways: Water and a splash of milk
Add nuts or seeds for more protein
dishes.pair: Berries, banana or a spoon of peanut butter.
dishes.mp: Keeps 3 days in the fridge. Reheat with a splash of milk.
light: Use water for half the milk
prot: Stir in Greek yogurt or a scoop of protein powder

dishes.n: Bangers and mash with onion gravy
dishes.d: Grilled sausages on creamy mash with onion gravy and peas.
steps: Grill or bake the sausages at 400°F (200°C) for 25 minutes, turning once.
Boil the potatoes 15 minutes, drain and mash with milk, butter and salt.
Cook the onions in a little pan until soft and golden, sprinkle in the flour and stir 1 minute.
Add the stock gradually and simmer until it makes a gravy.
Cook the peas and serve everything together.
dishes.mp: Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
light: Use 1 tbsp butter total and half the gravy

dishes.d: Slow-baked lamb and onion stew under a layer of sliced potato.
steps: Brown the lamb in oil and layer in a casserole with the onions and carrots.
Add stock, bay leaves and thyme.
Cover with overlapping potato slices and brush with butter.
Bake covered at 340°F (170°C) for 1 hour 30 minutes.
Uncover and bake 30 minutes more until the potatoes are golden.
ways: Add Worcestershire sauce for a deeper flavour
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes 3 months.
light: Use less butter and extra carrots

dishes.d: Thick Spanish omelette of potato and onion, served with a green salad.
steps: Cook the potatoes and onion in the olive oil over low heat 15 minutes until soft but not browned. Drain the excess oil.
Beat the eggs with salt and fold in the potatoes and onion.
Cook in a nonstick pan 5 minutes over medium-low heat until set underneath.
Flip with a plate and cook 3 more minutes.
Slice and serve warm or at room temperature with salad.
dishes.pair: Crusty bread, tomato salad or aioli.
dishes.mp: Keeps 3 days in the fridge and is good cold.
light: Drain the potatoes well and use 3 tbsp oil
prot: Add a side of ham or tuna

dishes.d: Cold Andalusian tomato and cucumber soup, finished with olive oil.
ing: 2 slices day-old bread, soaked in water
steps: Roughly chop the tomatoes, cucumber and pepper.
Blend with the bread, garlic and vinegar until very smooth.
Slowly add the olive oil while blending.
Season with salt and chill at least 2 hours.
Serve cold, with diced cucumber or pepper on top if you like.
ways: Chunky with diced vegetables on top
Add watermelon for a summer version
dishes.pair: Crusty bread or a boiled egg.
dishes.mp: Keeps 3 days in the fridge. Stir before serving.
prot: Top with chopped egg and serrano ham

dishes.d: Chicken thighs browned and simmered with plenty of garlic and white wine.
ing: 0.5 cup dry white wine or stock
steps: Season the chicken and brown in olive oil 4 minutes a side. Remove.
Add the garlic and chilli to the same pan and cook 1 minute without burning.
Pour in the wine and scrape up the browned bits.
Return the chicken, cover and simmer 15 minutes.
Finish with parsley.
ways: Use breast for a leaner dish
dishes.pair: Rice, bread or potatoes (add 150–250 calories for the side).
dishes.mp: Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
light: Use 3 tbsp oil and skinless chicken breast

dishes.d: Sizzling prawns in garlic, chilli and olive oil, with bread to mop up the oil.
ing: 2 dried chillies or 1 tsp chilli flakes
steps: Warm the oil with the garlic and chilli over low heat 3 minutes.
Turn the heat up and add the prawns with salt.
Cook 2–3 minutes until pink.
Add the sherry and parsley and cook 30 seconds.
Serve straight away with bread.
ways: Use smaller portions of oil and more bread-free sides
dishes.pair: Crusty bread or a green salad.
dishes.mp: Best fresh. Doesn't reheat well.
light: Use 3 tbsp oil and one slice of bread

dishes.d: Slow-cooked white bean stew with chorizo, smoked pork and saffron.
ing: 1.5 cups dried fabes or white beans, soaked overnight
4 oz smoked pork shoulder or ham hock meat
steps: Cook the onion and garlic in oil 5 minutes, add the paprika and stir.
Add the soaked beans, chorizo, smoked pork, saffron, bay leaves and enough water to cover by 1 inch.
Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer gently 1 hour 30 minutes until the beans are creamy.
Don't stir hard; shake the pot instead so the beans don't break.
Season with salt at the end and slice the meats to serve.
dishes.pair: A green salad and crusty bread.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes 3 months.
light: Use 2 oz chorizo and skim the fat

dishes.d: Madrid's chickpea stew with chicken, chorizo, potatoes and vegetables.
ing: 12 oz bone-in chicken thighs or beef shank
steps: Put the chickpeas, meat, chorizo and onion in a large pot with water and bring to a boil. Skim.
Simmer gently 1 hour.
Add the potatoes, carrots and cabbage.
Cook 30 minutes more until everything is tender.
Serve the broth first, then the chickpeas, vegetables and meat together.
ways: Skip the chorizo for a leaner stew
dishes.pair: A little of the broth as a first course.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes 3 months.
light: Skip the chorizo and use skinless chicken

dishes.d: Spanish ratatouille of tomato, peppers and courgette, served with a fried egg.
steps: Cook the onion in the oil 5 minutes, add the peppers and cook 8 minutes.
Add the aubergine and courgette and cook 10 minutes.
Pour in the tomatoes, season and simmer 15 minutes until thick.
Crack in the eggs, cover and cook 4 minutes until set, or serve fried eggs on top.
Serve hot.
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes 3 months without the egg.
prot: Add a slice of crusty bread and a second egg

dishes.d: Hake in a garlic and parsley sauce with peas.
steps: Warm the oil and cook the garlic 1 minute without browning.
Whisk the cornflour into the stock and add with the parsley and peas.
Simmer 3 minutes.
Lay the hake in the sauce, cover and cook 6–8 minutes.
Swirl the pan to bring the sauce together and serve.
ways: Add clams for a Basque version
dishes.mp: Best fresh. Fish keeps 2 days.

dishes.d: Grilled chicken on crisp romaine with Parmesan, croutons and Caesar dressing.
steps: Rub the chicken with oil, salt and pepper and grill 6 minutes a side until cooked through. Rest and slice.
Toss the romaine with dressing and a squeeze of lemon.
Top with Parmesan and croutons.
Add the sliced chicken.
Serve right away.
dishes.mp: Dress just before serving. Chicken keeps 3 days.
light: Use 2 tbsp dressing and skip the croutons
prot: Add extra chicken or a boiled egg

dishes.n: Turkey burger with sweet potato fries
dishes.d: Lean turkey burger on a whole-wheat bun with baked sweet potato fries.
ing: 1.5 lb sweet potatoes, cut in fries
lettuce, tomato, onion, mustard, salt, pepper
steps: Toss the sweet potato with oil and salt and bake at 425°F (220°C) for 30 minutes, turning once.
Mix the turkey with egg, breadcrumbs, salt and pepper and shape into 4 patties.
Grill or pan-cook 5–6 minutes a side until cooked through (165°F / 74°C).
Toast the buns.
Build with lettuce, tomato, onion and mustard.
dishes.mp: Patties keep 3 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen.
light: Skip the bun or serve a smaller portion of fries

dishes.d: Fluffy pancakes with berries and maple syrup.
steps: Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.
Whisk the buttermilk, eggs and melted butter, then stir into the dry mix until just combined.
Cook ¼-cup scoops in a lightly greased pan over medium heat until bubbles form, then flip.
Cook 1–2 minutes more until golden.
Serve with berries and syrup.
ways: Add a spoon of yogurt for extra protein
dishes.pair: Greek yogurt, berries or scrambled eggs.
dishes.mp: Cooked pancakes keep 3 days in the fridge or 2 months frozen.
light: Use 2 tbsp syrup and extra berries
prot: Serve with a side of eggs or Greek yogurt

dishes.d: Creamy potato and clam soup with bacon.
ing: 2 cans chopped clams (6.5 oz each), with juice
steps: Cook the bacon until crisp, remove and keep the fat.
Cook the onion and celery in the bacon fat and butter 5 minutes.
Stir in the flour, then the clam juice and milk gradually.
Add the potatoes and thyme and simmer 15 minutes until tender.
Add the clams and half-and-half and warm through 3 minutes.
dishes.pair: Oyster crackers or a green salad.
dishes.mp: Keeps 3 days in the fridge. Don't boil after adding clams.
light: Use semi-skimmed milk and no half-and-half

dishes.n: Chicken and sausage gumbo with rice
dishes.d: Louisiana stew built on a dark roux with chicken, andouille, okra and rice.
ing: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cubed
steps: Make the roux: cook the oil and flour over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, 15–20 minutes until the colour of milk chocolate.
Add the onion, pepper and celery and cook 5 minutes.
Add the chicken, sausage and seasoning and stir 3 minutes.
Add the stock and okra and simmer 30 minutes.
Cook the rice and serve the gumbo over it.
ways: Use less oil in the roux
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes 3 months.
light: Use a smaller portion of rice and less sausage

dishes.n: BBQ pulled pork sandwich with slaw
dishes.d: Slow-cooked pulled pork in barbecue sauce on a bun with crunchy slaw.
steps: Rub the pork with paprika, salt and pepper and place in a slow cooker or covered pot with the water.
Cook on low 8 hours or at 300°F (150°C) for 4 hours until it falls apart.
Shred the pork, discard the fat and mix with the barbecue sauce.
Mix the cabbage with mayonnaise and vinegar for the slaw.
Pile the pork and slaw on the buns.
ways: Serve without a bun on lettuce
dishes.pair: Corn on the cob or baked beans.
dishes.mp: Pork keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes 3 months.
light: Use a lettuce wrap or half a bun

dishes.d: Baked-style macaroni and cheese with a little cauliflower folded in.
steps: Boil the macaroni 2 minutes short of the packet time, adding the cauliflower for the last 3 minutes. Drain.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour 1 minute, then add the milk gradually and whisk until thick.
Stir in the cheese, mustard, salt and pepper until melted.
Fold in the pasta and cauliflower.
Serve, or top with breadcrumbs and bake 15 minutes at 375°F (190°C).
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Add a splash of milk when reheating.
light: Use half the cheese and double the cauliflower

dishes.d: Chicken, bacon, egg, avocado and blue cheese on greens with a red wine vinaigrette.
steps: Season and grill the chicken 6 minutes a side. Rest and dice.
Cook the bacon crisp and crumble.
Whisk the oil, vinegar, salt and pepper.
Arrange the romaine on a platter with rows of chicken, bacon, egg, avocado, tomato and cheese.
Drizzle with the vinaigrette.
ways: Use half the bacon and cheese
dishes.mp: Keep components separate: the salad keeps 3 days and avocado is added fresh.
light: Use half the bacon and cheese

dishes.d: Smashed avocado on wholegrain toast with two eggs.
steps: Toast the bread.
Mash the avocado with lemon, salt and pepper.
Fry or poach the eggs.
Spread the avocado on the toast.
Top with the eggs and chilli flakes.
dishes.mp: Make fresh. Avocado browns quickly.
light: Use poached eggs and 1 egg each
prot: Add smoked salmon or a side of Greek yogurt

dishes.d: Soft rice balls served in a rich peanut soup with chicken or goat.
steps: Boil the rice with extra water until very soft, then mash and beat until sticky. Shape into balls with wet hands.
Season and boil the meat with onion, ginger and salt until tender, keeping the stock.
Loosen the peanut butter with a cup of warm stock until smooth with no lumps.
Blend the tomatoes and pepper, add to the pot with the peanut mixture and the rest of the stock.
Simmer uncovered 25–30 minutes, skimming the oil that rises, until it thickens. Serve the balls in the soup.
ways: Use chicken breast for a lighter soup
Blend in a roasted red pepper for extra body
dishes.pair: Sliced avocado or a light cabbage salad.
dishes.mp: Soup keeps 4 days chilled, 2 months frozen. Make rice balls fresh.
light: Use 2/3 cup peanut butter, skinless chicken, skim the oil
prot: Add extra goat and a boiled egg

dishes.d: Spiced fried plantain cubes with ginger, pepper and cloves, served with roasted peanuts.
steps: Peel and cube the plantains.
Mix the ginger, cayenne, cloves, nutmeg and salt with 2 tbsp water and toss the cubes through it.
Let them sit 10 minutes so the spice sticks.
Fry in hot oil, or air-fry at 400°F (200°C) for 12–15 minutes, turning once, until deep gold.
Serve hot with the peanuts.
dishes.pair: Roasted peanuts, or on the side of waakye or grilled fish.
dishes.mp: Best fresh. Spice mix keeps a month in a jar.
light: Air-fry with 1 tbsp oil and skip the peanuts

dishes.d: Black-eyed peas stewed in palm oil and tomato, served with fried ripe plantain.
steps: Boil the soaked peas 35–45 minutes until tender but not mushy. Keep a cup of the liquid.
Heat the palm oil, fry the chopped onion 3 minutes, add tomato paste and fry 2 minutes.
Add the blended tomatoes and pepper, cook 12 minutes until thick and the oil separates.
Stir in the peas, crayfish and enough cooking liquid to loosen. Simmer 10 minutes and season.
Fry the plantain slices until golden and serve alongside.
ways: Vegetable oil for a lighter, less earthy version
Add smoked fish or turkey to the stew
dishes.pair: Fried plantain, gari, or a green salad.
dishes.mp: Stew keeps 5 days chilled and freezes well. Fry plantain fresh.
light: Use 1 tbsp oil and bake the plantain instead of frying
prot: Add smoked turkey and an egg

dishes.n: Ga kenkey with fried fish and shito
dishes.d: Fermented corn dough steamed in husks, served with fried fish, pepper sauce and onion.
steps: Steam or boil the kenkey balls 15 minutes until hot through.
Season the fish with salt and a little pepper and fry or grill 6 minutes a side.
Grind the tomato, pepper and half the onion coarsely for a fresh pepper.
Slice the rest of the onion raw.
Serve kenkey with fish, shito, fresh pepper and onion.
ways: With fried egg instead of fish
dishes.pair: Fresh tomato pepper, raw onion, avocado.
dishes.mp: Kenkey keeps a week chilled. Fry fish fresh.
light: Grill the fish, use 1 tbsp shito, half a ball of kenkey
prot: Two fish and an extra egg

dishes.d: A clear, peppery tomato broth with goat meat, served with pounded cassava and plantain fufu.
steps: Season the goat with salt, ginger and chopped onion and steam it in its own juices 10 minutes.
Add water and boil 45–60 minutes until the meat is tender.
Boil the tomatoes, remaining onion, pepper and garden eggs 10 minutes, then blend smooth.
Strain the blend into the pot, simmer 15 minutes and season.
Serve hot with fufu.
ways: Chicken or fish for a lighter soup
dishes.mp: Soup keeps 4 days, freezes 2 months. Fufu is best fresh.
light: Chicken breast, more broth and less fufu
prot: Extra goat and a side of boiled egg

dishes.d: Gari fried with tomato, onion and egg into a soft, savoury grain dish.
steps: Sprinkle the gari with about a cup of water and leave 5 minutes to swell, then fluff with a fork.
Heat the oil, fry the onion and pepper 3 minutes, add tomato paste and blended tomatoes, cook 10 minutes.
Scramble the eggs into the sauce.
Fold in the damp gari until evenly coloured and season.
Serve warm with avocado or fried plantain.
ways: Vegan: skip the egg and add beans
dishes.pair: Avocado, fried plantain, or a tomato salad.
dishes.mp: Keeps 2 days chilled. Reheat with a splash of water.
light: Use 1 tbsp oil and two eggs
prot: Four eggs and a side of beans

dishes.d: Afang leaves and waterleaf cooked with beef, dried fish and periwinkle in palm oil.
steps: Boil the beef with onion, pepper and salt until tender, keeping the stock.
Add the dried fish and periwinkle and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in the palm oil and crayfish and cook 5 minutes.
Add the waterleaf, cook 3 minutes, then the ground afang. Simmer 8 minutes without much extra water.
Season and serve with pounded yam.
dishes.mp: Soup keeps 4 days chilled, 3 months frozen.
light: 3 tbsp palm oil and a smaller yam portion

dishes.d: Shredded cassava dressed with palm oil, potash and ugba, with fish and garden eggs.
ing: salt and ehu seed to taste
steps: Soak the abacha in warm water 5 minutes until soft, then drain well.
Whisk the palm oil with the potash water until it turns thick and yellow.
Stir in the crayfish, pepper, salt and ground ehu.
Fold in the abacha, ugba, onion and flaked fish.
Serve at room temperature with garden eggs.
ways: Without potash: emulsify the oil with a little warm water
dishes.pair: Garden eggs, chilled palm wine or zobo.
dishes.mp: Best eaten the day it's made.
light: Use 3 tbsp palm oil and more garden eggs
prot: Add extra fish and a boiled egg

dishes.d: Cow foot in a thick spiced palm oil paste, served in a wooden bowl with onion and utazi.
steps: Boil the cow foot with salt, onion and pepper 50–60 minutes until tender.
Whisk the palm oil with the potash water until it thickens to a yellow paste.
Stir in the ground ehu, ground pepper and seasoning.
Fold the hot meat through the paste until well coated.
Top with sliced onion and utazi and serve warm.
ways: Less potash for a looser sauce
dishes.mp: Keeps 3 days chilled. Reheat gently so the oil doesn't split.
light: Use 3 tbsp palm oil and serve with plenty of vegetables

dishes.d: Soft rice pudding served with a baobab-leaf soup.
steps: Boil the rice with plenty of water until very soft, then mash and beat until smooth. Shape into balls.
Boil the beef with onion, dawadawa and salt until tender, keeping the stock.
Add the oil, ground pepper and crayfish to the stock and simmer 10 minutes.
Sprinkle in the kuka powder while stirring so it doesn't clump, and simmer 5 minutes.
Season and serve with the tuwo.
dishes.mp: Soup keeps 4 days. Make the tuwo fresh.
light: Smaller tuwo portion and lean beef
prot: Extra beef and a boiled egg

dishes.d: Smoky grilled goat tossed in a hot pepper and onion sauce.
steps: Season the goat with salt, curry, thyme and half an onion and boil 35 minutes until tender.
Grill or roast the pieces at 425°F (220°C) for 15 minutes until the edges char.
Blend the bell peppers and scotch bonnets coarsely.
Heat the oil, fry the sliced onion 2 minutes, add the pepper blend and cook 8 minutes.
Toss the grilled goat through the sauce and serve hot.
ways: Chicken or turkey instead of goat
dishes.pair: Cold drinks, fried plantain, or rice.
dishes.mp: Keeps 3 days chilled. Reheat in a hot pan.
light: Use 1 tbsp oil and trim the fat

dishes.d: Soft mashed beans under a dark, sweet-hot fried pepper sauce.
ing: 2 cups honey beans or black-eyed peas
steps: Boil the beans 60–70 minutes until they collapse, adding water as needed, then mash roughly and salt.
Soak the dried peppers in hot water 20 minutes, then blend with one onion.
Heat the palm oil, fry the second onion slowly 10 minutes until very dark.
Add the pepper blend and fry 20 minutes on low until thick, dark and sweet-smelling. Season with salt and sugar.
Spoon the sauce over the beans and serve with bread or plantain.
ways: Vegetable oil for a milder sauce
Serve with agege bread or boiled yam
dishes.pair: Agege bread, fried plantain, boiled yam.
dishes.mp: Beans and sauce both keep 4 days and freeze well.
light: Use 2 tbsp oil for the sauce
prot: Add boiled eggs and fried fish

dishes.d: Finely pounded cassava leaves simmered with palm oil, beef, fish and peanut.
steps: Boil the beef with onion and salt until tender, keeping the stock.
Add the cassava leaves and 2 cups of stock and simmer 25 minutes.
Stir in the palm oil, peanut butter and smoked fish.
Simmer 20 minutes more on low, stirring so it doesn't catch, until dark and thick.
Season and serve over white rice.
ways: Without peanut for a lighter stew
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days chilled and freezes 3 months. Better the next day.
light: 3 tbsp palm oil, no peanut butter, more rice vegetables

dishes.d: Light, quick-cooking West African grain with a tomato and vegetable sauce.
steps: Rinse the fonio, then steam or simmer with the water 5–8 minutes until fluffy. Fork through.
Fry the onion in the oil 3 minutes.
Add the blended tomatoes and pepper and cook 10 minutes.
Add the chopped vegetables and simmer 10 minutes until just tender.
Season and serve over the fonio.
ways: Add beans or fish for protein
dishes.pair: Grilled fish, beans, or a green salad.
dishes.mp: Keeps 3 days. Fonio reheats best steamed.

dishes.d: Crisp black-eyed pea fritters with smooth fermented corn porridge.
steps: Soak the peas 2 hours, rub off the skins and drain.
Blend with the onion, pepper and as little water as possible into a thick batter.
Whisk the batter hard for 3 minutes so it lightens and holds air, then salt it.
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil and fry 4 minutes until deep gold. Drain on a rack.
Mix the pap with cold water, pour in boiling water while stirring until it thickens, and serve with the akara.
ways: Bake at 400°F for 18 minutes for a softer fritter
dishes.mp: Batter keeps a day chilled. Fry fresh; akara goes soft quickly.
light: Air-fry the akara and take the pap without sugar
prot: Add a boiled egg and take the pap with milk

dishes.n: Nyama choma with ugali and kachumbari
dishes.d: Slow-grilled goat with stiff maize meal and a sharp tomato-onion salad.
ing: 2 lb goat meat on the bone
steps: Rub the goat with salt and grill slowly over low coals 40–50 minutes, turning often.
Boil the water, rain in the maize meal while stirring hard.
Keep beating 10–15 minutes until it pulls away from the pot, then turn out and shape.
Dice the tomato, onion, chilli and coriander and dress with lime and salt for the kachumbari.
Chop the goat and serve with ugali and salad.
ways: Oven at 325°F for 90 minutes then finish under the broiler
Chicken or beef instead of goat
dishes.mp: Meat keeps 3 days. Ugali is best fresh; reheat with steam.
light: Trim the fat, smaller ugali portion, double kachumbari
prot: Extra goat and a side of beans

dishes.d: Collard greens fried with onion and tomato, the everyday side that stretches the week.
steps: Fry the onion in the oil 3 minutes.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook 5 minutes until soft.
Add the greens and a splash of water, cover and cook 8–10 minutes until tender.
Season with salt and cumin.
Make the ugali as usual and serve together.
dishes.mp: Greens keep 3 days chilled.
light: 1 tbsp oil and a smaller ugali portion

dishes.d: Steamed green bananas mashed soft, served in a peanut sauce.
steps: Peel the bananas under running water with oiled hands and cut into chunks.
Steam wrapped in banana leaves or in a covered pot 30 minutes until very soft, then mash.
Fry the onion in the oil, add the chopped tomatoes and cook 8 minutes.
Loosen the peanut butter with warm water and stir it in. Simmer 10 minutes.
Season and serve the sauce over the matoke.
ways: Add beef or smoked fish to the sauce
dishes.mp: Keeps 3 days. Reheat with a splash of water.
light: 1/3 cup peanut butter and 1 tsp oil
prot: Add beef and a boiled egg

dishes.d: Smooth spiced chickpea flour stew, the everyday fasting dish, eaten with injera.
ing: 1 cup shiro powder (chickpea flour with berbere)
steps: Fry the onion slowly in the oil 10 minutes without browning it hard.
Add the garlic and berbere and fry 2 minutes.
Whisk the shiro powder into the water until smooth, then pour it in while stirring.
Simmer 12–15 minutes, stirring often, until it thickens and loses the raw flour taste.
Season and serve on injera.
ways: Niter kibbeh for a richer stew
Add chopped tomato for a fresher finish
dishes.mp: Keeps 4 days and thickens; loosen with water when reheating.
prot: Add lentil wat and a boiled egg

dishes.d: Deep red chicken stew built on a very slow-cooked onion base and berbere.
steps: Rub the chicken with lemon juice and salt and set aside.
Cook the onions dry in a heavy pot 20–25 minutes, stirring, until they collapse and darken.
Add the butter or oil, garlic, ginger and berbere and cook 10 minutes.
Add 2 cups of water and the chicken, cover and simmer 40 minutes.
Score the boiled eggs, add them for the last 10 minutes, and season.
ways: Halve the berbere for less heat
dishes.mp: Better the next day. Keeps 4 days, freezes 3 months.
light: Skinless chicken, 2 tbsp oil, one injera

dishes.d: Spicy vegetable and bean relish served with stiff maize pap.
steps: Fry the onion and chilli in the oil 4 minutes.
Add the curry powder and cook 1 minute, then the carrot and pepper for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cook 8 minutes until saucy.
Stir in the beans and warm through. Season.
Make the pap and serve together.
ways: Without beans as a pure vegetable relish
dishes.mp: Keeps 5 days chilled and tastes better on day two.
light: 1 tbsp oil and a smaller pap portion

dishes.d: Maize nsima with grilled lake fish and pumpkin leaves in tomato.
steps: Make a thin porridge with 1 cup of flour and the water, then beat in the rest until very stiff.
Shape the nsima with a wet spoon.
